title: I MYSELF WILL DRIVE THEM OUT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "the area of the Byblians on the north, and all the region of Lebanon to the east, from Baal Gad below Mount Hermon to Lebo Hamath. As for all the inhabitants of the mountain regions from Lebanon to Misrephoth Maim, that is, all the Sidonians, I myself will drive them out before the Israelites. Be sure to allocate this land to Israel for an inheritance, as I have instructed you" - Josh 13:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the heart of the promise: "I myself will drive them out before the Israelites." The land that still remained was not something Israel had to conquer by sheer effort. God took personal responsibility. He would go ahead of them and do what they could not do for themselves.

This is the beautiful pattern all through Scripture. God gives the command — "allocate this land" — and God supplies the power — "I myself will drive them out." Israel's part was to trust and to act; God's part was to give the victory. The work was a partnership, but the strength was always His.

We can grow so weary trying to change ourselves and our circumstances by willpower alone. This verse invites us to rest in a God who says, "I myself will do it." Sanctification, the slow work of becoming more like Jesus, is not something we manufacture on our own. It is God who works in us both to will and to act according to His good purpose (Phil 2:13). We take the ground by trusting the God who has promised to go before us. Our confidence is never in our own strength but in the One who fights on our behalf.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you trying to change something by willpower that only God can do?
- What would it look like to trust the God who says "I myself will drive them out"?
- Where do you need to move forward in faith while resting in His strength?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I grow tired trying to change in my own strength. Thank You that You Yourself go before me. Help me to trust Your power and step forward in faith. Amen.
